newsitem.title: USA: Theo Wilson, celebrated trial reporter, dies.
newsitem.headline: Theo Wilson, celebrated trial reporter, dies.

text.p: Theo Wilson, a reporter who covered many of America's most sensational trials for The New York Daily News, died at a Los Angeles hospital Friday, friends said. She was 78.

Wilson was taken to Cedars-Sinai Medical Centre in Los Angeles Thursday and died in the early hours of Friday of a cerebral haemorrhage, said Carolyn Fox, executive director of the Radio and Television News Association of Southern California and a friend of Wilson.

Between the 1950s and the 1980s, Wilson covered many of America's most celebrated trials for The New York Daily News, winning many journalism awards. She retired from the Daily News in 1984 but continued to write about trials, including columns about the O.J. Simpson trial.

Among the famous trials she covered were those of Dr. Sam Sheppard, who was accused of murdering his pregnant wife; Jack Ruby, who shot Lee Harvey Oswald, accused assassin of President John Kennedy, and cult leader Charles Manson.

Wilson died just two days after the publication of her book "Headline Justice", containing her reminiscences of the high-profile trials she covered. She had scheduled tv appearances and book signings this week to promote her book.
